data.title: Paytm snaps 2-day losing run on S'pore investment plan; Nomura retains Buy
data.description:
Paytm share price target: Shares of Paytm parent One 97 Communications surged over 2.5 per cent in trade on Friday, snapping a two-session losing streak, after the company announced that its Singapore arm would invest up to ₹200 crore in subsidiaries of Singapore-based Funding Societies, including about ₹162 crore for a 19.1 per cent stake in its payments subsidiary CardUp.
 
Paytm shares opened higher at ₹1,730 and extended gains to hit an intraday high of ₹1,770.30 on the National Stock Exchange (NSE).
 
In the previous two trading sessions, the stock had declined over 9 per cent amid reports that the proposed implementation of the Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) on UPI transactions could be delayed further.
 
 
As the session progressed, Paytm shares pared most of their early gains. As of 11:35 AM, the stock was trading 0.45 per cent higher at ₹1,734 on the NSE.
 
Paytm shares have jumped 35 per cent in 2026 so far, compared with a 2.3 per cent decline in the Nifty 50 index. From 2026 low of ₹930.60, touched on March 30, the stock has bounced back over 85 per cent. The stock touched an all-time high of ₹1,960 on November 13. 
Paytm invests ₹200cr in funding societies, buys CardUp stake
 
According to a regulatory filing, the board of Paytm Singapore Pte Ltd on Thursday approved a partnership with Funding Asia Group Pte Ltd (Funding Societies).
 
The initial investment of about ₹162 crore will be made in cash for the issuance of shares in CardUp Pte Ltd, a payments subsidiary of Funding Societies. The remaining investment of about Rs₹38 crore may be made in one of Funding Societies' affiliates. Paytm expects the CardUp transaction to be completed by May 20, 2027.
 
One 97 Communications will also enter into a business and technology partnership with CardUp, under which it will provide payments and lending technology to the Singapore firm to expand Paytm's technology-led payments and financial services stack in Singapore. The company will receive technology fees and a revenue share under the agreement, which will be initially valid for five years with a right of renewal on mutually acceptable terms.
 
CardUp, incorporated in October 2015, is a Singapore-based digital payments company (a subsidiary of Funding Asia Group).  
Paytm share price target 
Following this, Nomura has maintained 'Buy' rating on Paytm stock, with a target price of ₹2,300. The target implies an upside of 33 per cent from the previous close of ₹1,725.90. 
 
The brokerage said that it expects Paytm to continue to target select international markets in a measured way, leveraging its proven technology stack in merchant payments and financial services.
 
Nomura believes that the investment is small relative to Paytm's balance sheet and is unlikely to change its financials materially in the near term. It is a low-cost way to enter the Singapore market.

data.title: CEC appointment law: SC declines separate hearing to recall split verdict
data.description:
The Supreme Court on Friday declined a submission to separately list a plea seeking recall of a split verdict delivered by a two-judge bench on whether challenges to the 2023 law governing the appointment of the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) and Election Commissioners (ECs) should be referred to a larger bench.

A bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said the recall application, as well as any challenge to the reference order, could be considered by the five-judge Constitution bench already constituted to hear the batch of petitions challenging the validity of the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023.

 

The CJI also said the five-judge bench could consider the recall application even after the retirement of one of the judges who delivered the split verdict.

Bhushan said that the recall application should be listed before the original bench comprising Justices Dipankar Datta and Satish Chandra Sharma, which delivered the split verdict on September 23.

He pointed out that Justice Sharma was due to retire next week. Bhushan further said that Justice Sharma had a conflict of interest and, therefore, the application seeking recall of the verdict ought to be heard by the same bench.

When the CJI suggested that the reference bench could consider the application, Bhushan said the reference order itself was recalled on the ground of an alleged conflict of interest.

However, the CJI said that the issue could be raised before the five-judge Constitution bench, which has been constituted for final adjudication of the constitutional challenge to the 2023 law.

The development follows a split verdict delivered on September 23 by Justices Datta and Sharma on whether the petitions challenging the 2023 law warranted consideration by a larger bench.

The main objection was the exclusion of the CJI from the panel to select the CEC and ECs. The panel now includes the prime minister, the leader of opposition in Lok Sabha and a cabinet minister.

While Justice Datta was of the view that the challenge could be adjudicated by a two-judge bench, Justice Sharma favoured a reference to a five-judge Constitution bench, considering the significant constitutional questions involved.

data.title: Trading still anchors NSE's business as clearing section gains share
data.description:
NSE went public in September via an offer for sale, marking a significant milestone for the country’s largest stock exchange. Its results for the second quarter of the financial year (Q2 FY27), compared with the same period last year, show that its clearing services business grew faster than its dominant trading business in terms of revenue. Clearing revenue rose 13.74 per cent to ₹464.88 crore, against a 9.34 per cent increase in trading revenue to ₹3,603.99 crore. The “others” segment recorded the fastest growth of 32.54 per cent, taking its revenue to ₹211.95 crore. 
 
Trading’s profit surged 157.25 per cent to ₹2,496.21 crore in Q2 FY27, compared with ₹970.36 crore a year ago. The clearing services segment’s profit increased by just 3.34 per cent to ₹280.09 crore from ₹271.05 crore, while “others” grew 49.50 per cent to ₹117.28 crore. Despite clearing's faster revenue growth, trading continued to generate the bulk of segment profitability, with its result rising much more sharply during the quarter. 
 
Trading’s share of gross segment revenue (total segment revenue excluding revenue from other sources) declined from 85.29 per cent in Q2 FY26 to 84.19 per cent in Q2 FY27, while clearing’s share increased from 10.58 per cent to 10.86 per cent. “Others” also gained ground, with its revenue contribution rising from 4.14 per cent to 4.95 per cent. While trading remains overwhelmingly dominant, the rising contribution of clearing and other services suggests a gradual broadening of NSE’s revenue base.

data.title: US lawmakers introduce bill after Indian origin grandmother's deportation
data.description:
A Sikh grandmother's deportation to India after three decades of stay in the US has prompted four California lawmakers to introduce a bill in the US Congress to protect long-term immigrant residents.

The Protect Our Neighbours Act, introduced by Congressman John Garamendi, draws inspiration from the deportation of Harjit Kaur, a resident of the San Francisco Bay Area, by the Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) last year.

The draft legislation has also received support from representatives Lateefah Simon, Zoe Lofgren, and Juan Vargas.

"The Protect Our Neighbours Act would provide people, like Ms. Kaur who worked in my district for decades, with a fair opportunity to move beyond a final order of removal and continue building futures here in the US where they have made their homes and families," Simon said.

 

Garamendi said nearly one year ago, ICE cruelly detained and deported Kaur, a 73-year-old grandmother with no criminal record - who faithfully reported to ICE every six months for more than 13 years.

Her cruel and unreasonable detention and deportation is just one more example of the thousands of individuals across the country whose lives and families have been upended by President Donald Trump's ICE, Garamendi said.

According to the American Immigration Council, roughly 1.19 million people with removal orders remain in the US, many having spent years building lives, raising families, and working here.

Under President Trump, the Department of Homeland Security and ICE have aggressively pursued individuals with final removal orders, regardless of how long the case had been deferred, putting long-term residents who have routinely complied with check-ins at renewed risk of detention and deportation.

The bill seeks to make final removal orders expire 10 years after issuance.

An immigration judge could renew an expired order at the Homeland Security Secretary's request, but only with clear and convincing evidence of significant reasons for the delay unrelated to administrative or funding problems, and new evidence establishing that renewal served the public interest.

People with expired, unrenewed orders could seek lawful status for which they qualify after at least 10 years' continuous US presence, provided they had no conviction for an offence punishable by more than a year in prison.

Renewal would be barred while that petition was pending. A separate provision would allow discretionary permanent residence for certain people physically present in the US with longstanding orders based on specified immigration grounds.

data.title: H-1B visa workers' children could get Green Card pathway under this US Bill
data.description:
US House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries on Wednesday pledged to push legislation that could offer a pathway to permanent residency for eligible children of Indian H-1B visa holders, saying Congress should act on the measure during its current session or take it up early in the next Congress.
 
The American Dream and Promise Act of 2025 proposes a route to lawful permanent residence, or a Green Card, for certain immigrants who came to the US as children. These include eligible children of foreign workers admitted under H-1B, L-1, E-1 and E-2 visa categories.
 
Jeffries called for the legislation to be passed during the current Congress, referring to an effort by Representative Sylvia Garcia of Texas to force a House vote on the measure.
  
“I can guarantee you that if that doesn’t happen, we’re going to move the Dream and Promise Act in the next Congress, early in the next Congress,” he told reporters at a news conference.
 
Asked whether he had spoken to President Donald Trump about a possible immigration agreement, Jeffries said: “Haven’t heard from the President yet.”
 
He described the legislation as the starting point for broader immigration reforms. “We should start with the Dream and Promise Act, but that’s the beginning. That’s not the end,” he said.
 
What the American Dream and Promise Act proposes
 
The legislation seeks to address the immigration difficulties faced by young people who grew up in the US but risk losing their legal status when they turn 21.
 
Many are children of foreign professionals who entered the country on temporary work visas, including H-1B visas. They lived in the US as dependants, attended American schools and universities, and built their lives there. However, lengthy employment-based Green Card backlogs can prevent their parents from securing permanent residency before they turn 21.
 
Under existing rules, these children generally lose their dependent status at 21, a situation commonly referred to as 'ageing out'. They are often described as 'documented Dreamers'.
 
Section 102 of the proposed legislation expressly includes eligible sons and daughters of individuals admitted under the E-1, E-2, H-1B and L-1 non-immigrant visa categories.
 
What are the proposed eligibility conditions?
 
Under the Bill's Dream Act provisions, eligible applicants would be able to obtain conditional permanent resident status for 10 years, subject to requirements relating to their age at entry, continuous residence, education or employment, and background checks.
 
The proposed eligibility conditions include:
 
< Having entered the US at the age of 18 or younger.
< Having maintained continuous physical presence in the country since January 1, 2021.
< Having a US high school diploma or equivalent, being admitted to a college or post-secondary career and technical education programme, or currently being enrolled in school.
< Clearing criminal background and national security checks.
< Meeting Selective Service registration requirements, where applicable.
 
Eligible applicants could subsequently have the conditions on their residency removed and obtain lawful permanent resident status. They could then become eligible to apply for US citizenship after meeting the applicable residency requirements.
 
The Bill also proposes a pathway to permanent residency for certain individuals covered by Temporary Protected Status (TPS) and Deferred Enforced Departure (DED), subject to specified eligibility conditions and application deadlines. It also seeks to remove certain federal restrictions on states providing higher education benefits to undocumented students based on state residency.
 
Why travel could matter for applicants
 
Immigration attorney Steven Brown has cautioned prospective applicants against overlooking the Bill's proposed travel restrictions.
 
In a blog post, Brown said Section 304 sets out separate tests for continuous physical presence and continuous residence.
 
Under the proposed provisions, a single trip outside the US lasting more than 90 days, or overseas trips totalling more than 180 days, could break continuous physical presence.
 
The continuous residence requirement has a separate threshold: a single trip lasting more than 180 days could break residence unless the applicant can establish that they did not abandon their US residence.
 
This could affect young people who travel abroad for extended periods, including those spending a semester overseas or visiting family for a prolonged summer break.
 
The provisions remain part of proposed legislation and would not confer any immigration benefit unless the Bill is passed and enacted.

data.title: Flipkart's Big Billion Days sale timing weighs on Walmart's Q3 growth
data.description:
US-based retail giant Walmart has said it faced a 100-basis-point headwind to its top-line growth in the third quarter as the 'Big Billion Days' sales event of its Indian e-commerce arm Flipkart shifted to the fourth quarter this year.

"Timing of Flipkart's Big Billion Days ("BBD") event negatively affected growth with an expected corresponding benefit to Q4," said Walmart in its earnings statement.

The company saw the impact as Flipkart's 11-day Big Billion Days (BBD) festive sale shifted to a different timing compared with that of the previous year, with its sales contribution shifting to Walmart's fourth-quarter results.

"As we previewed on last quarter's call, we faced a 100-basis-point headwind to top-line growth in Q3 due to the timing of Flipkart's Big Billion Days event, or BBD in India, which will be reported in International's fourth-quarter results this year," said John David Rainey, Executive Vice President & Chief Financial Officer, Walmart Inc.

 

The 13th edition of Big Billion Days, which opened on October 9, 2026, recorded 20-22 per cent year-on-year growth in orders, units and buyers, according to reports.

However, Walmart also said this shift will provide a boost of around 100 basis points to its sales growth in the ongoing fourth quarter. The impact is expected to reverse in the December quarter, when the sales contribution from the event will be reflected in Walmart's international segment.

In the third quarter, Walmart, which follows the February-January fiscal calendar, said, "Timing of BBD negatively affected net sales growth by about 500 bps" in its international business, which operates in 18 countries outside the US, including India.

Walmart International's "e-commerce sales down 2 per cent and advertising business down 15 per cent, both negatively affected by timing of BBD," said the Bentonville, Arkansas-headquartered retail giant in its earnings statement for the third quarter of FY27.

In the zone, excluding Flipkart, inventory is growing slower than sales, it added.

Walmart International has reported a growth of 7 per cent to $35.9 billion in the third quarter of FY27. In terms of constant currency, Walmart International's growth was only 3.3 per cent to $34.7 billion.

"Growth driven primarily by India and China, with business mix benefits, partially offset by strategic investments in Mexico and Canada," it said.

The overall revenue of Walmart Inc. was $188.8 billion, up 5.2 per cent in Q3 FY27.

Walmart has also raised its full-year FY27 net sales growth outlook to 4.9-5.2 per cent, in constant currency, from its earlier estimate of 4-5 per cent.

"Net sales for FY27 are expected to grow 4.9 per cent to 5.2 per cent and adjusted operating income to grow 8 per cent to 8.6 per cent, all in constant currency," it said.

data.title: NSE shares jump 3% to fresh high; JM Financial sees MSCI entry in March
data.description:
NSE share price: Shares of the National Stock Exchange (NSE) were up for the third straight session on Friday, gaining nearly 3 per cent in intraday trading. The improving Indian stock market sentiment is creating a favourable environment for exchanges as stronger trading activity brightens their earnings outlook.
 
NSE's share price hit a fresh high of 2,251 on the BSE, up 2.8 per cent over its last close of ₹2,188.30. It has gained 26 per cent over its initial public offering (IPO) price of ₹1,785.  
 
This week alone, the stock has gained 13 per cent, which has pushed the market capitalisation (m-cap) of India's largest exchange above the ₹5.5 trillion mark. This has helped NSE pip Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC) to emerge as the ninth most-valuable Indian company. Currently, LIC is valued at ₹5.13 trillion. 
ALSO READ: Capital Markets: Derivatives surge on volatility; cash, MF flows stay muted
 
 
Domestic brokerage Motilal Oswal Financial Services (MOFSL) earlier this month said that NSE is well positioned to benefit from the structural deepening of India’s capital markets, with market capitalization-to-GDP at 131 per cent and demat penetration at just 17 per cent of the population.
 
Further, it noted that rising financial literacy, digital onboarding and participation from younger investors provide a long runway for trading activity growth.
 
NSE has a dominant market position, which provides a strong competitive moat. With favorable CAS modifications from Dec 2026, MOFSL expects derivatives volume recovery, while its scalable technology infrastructure and high trading capacity reinforce its leadership. "Diversification into non-transaction revenues and operating leverage should strengthen earnings visibility, with colocation, data feeds and clearing providing recurring income streams," it said, adding that it expects revenue/EBITDA/PAT to grow at 12 per cent/13 per cent/13 per cent CAGR over FY26–29, with EBITDA margins reaching ~77 per cent.
 

NSE to make MSCI debut in March: JM Financial

Additionally, JM Financial, in a note dated November 19, said NSE remains a highly probable candidate to enter the MSCI India Standard Index, scheduled to be announced in February 2027. Meanwhile, the changes will take effect in March 2027. 
ALSO READ: NSE deploys liquid cooling for AI infra, plans over 80 GPUs this quarter
 
After screening the entire India EQS universe and recent reshuffle against the indicative MSCI thresholds, we identified NSE, listed on September 24, 2026 with around $45 billion market capitalisation at listing, as far above the minimum size requirement and liquidity metrics, said JM Financial analyst Abhishek Kumar. It was not eligible in November 2026 because it was shy of MSCI's three-month minimum trading history at implementation.
 
If included, NSE could witness $1,511 million in passive inflows, as per the brokerage's estimates.
 
MSCI potential inclusions (Feb 2027)
 
Other stocks that have a high possibility of entering the MSCI index are: Ather Energy, Glenmark Pharma, Kalyan Jeweller and UNO Minda.

data.title: Centre notifies revised disability assessment norms for 8 categories
data.description:
The Centre has notified revised guidelines for assessing eight categories of specified disabilities under the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016, replacing the norms issued in March 2024.

The guidelines, issued by the Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities on November 18, cover locomotor disability, visual impairment, hearing impairment and speech and language disability, specific learning disability, intellectual disability and autism spectrum disorder, mental illness, blood disorder, multiple disorder and chronic neurological disorder.

For locomotor disabilities, assessment of the upper extremities covers the arm and hand, including range of motion, muscle strength, coordinated activities, prehension and sensation.

Conditions covered include amputation, cerebral palsy, leprosy-cured persons, dwarfism, muscular dystrophy and spinal deformities.

 

Except in cases of amputation, temporary disability certificates will be issued after six months of symptoms. Permanent certificates will be issued after the age of 18, with reassessment every 10 years where requested by the person with disability or recommended by a subject expert.

Dwarfism is defined as an adult height of less than 147 cm (4 feet 8 inches). Every one-inch reduction in vertical height attracts four per cent permanent physical impairment, while associated skeletal deformities are assessed separately.

Blindness includes total absence of sight, visual acuity (measure of how clearly eyes can see) below 3/60 in the better eye after best possible correction, or a field of vision of less than 10 degrees. Low vision covers visual acuity below 6/18 up to 3/60, or a field of vision below 40 degrees up to 10 degrees.

Hearing impairment is assessed through Pure Tone Audiometry, with hearing thresholds measured at 500, 1,000, 2,000 and 4,000 Hz. Speech and language disability assessment covers conditions such as laryngectomy, glossectomy, bilateral vocal cord paralysis, dysarthria and apraxia of speech.

The latter two are assessed after one year of regular documented speech therapy by registered speech-language pathologists.

For intellectual disability, assessment considers intellectual functioning and adaptive behaviour. The disability percentage is 25 per cent for borderline, 50 per cent for mild, 75 per cent for moderate, 90 per cent for severe and 100 per cent for profound intellectual disability.

The minimum age for certification is one completed year. Children above one year and up to five years will be diagnosed with Global Developmental Delay, while those above five years will be assessed for intellectual disability.

Specific learning disability covers difficulties in reading, written expression and mathematics. These must persist for at least six months despite targeted, evidence-based intervention. Assessment requires an IQ score of 85 or above.

The NIMHANS battery and NIEPID Grade Level Assessment Instrument for Schools are prescribed for children up to 18 years, while the NIEPID Adult Assessment Tool for Specific Learning Disability is prescribed for adults.

Autism spectrum disorder is diagnosed using the AIIMS-modified INCLEN tool. Children below six years will receive a diagnosis of moderate autism and a temporary certificate, with reassessment at six years or above.

For those aged six years and above, the disability percentage is 40 per cent for an Indian Scale for Assessment of Autism (ISAA) score of 70, 50 per cent for scores between 71 and 88, 60 per cent for 89-106, 70 per cent for 107-123, 80 per cent for 124-140, 90 per cent for 141-153 and 100 per cent for scores above 153. A score below 70 indicates no autism.

Mental illness is assessed through a psychiatrist's clinical examination and the Indian Disability Evaluation and Assessment Scale, which covers self-care, interpersonal activities, communication and understanding, and work.

The disability percentage is 25 per cent for mild, 55 per cent for moderate, 85 per cent for severe and 100 per cent for profound disability.

A minimum illness duration of two years is required for permanent certification. For illness lasting less than two years, a time-valid certificate may be issued, though severe or profound cases may be considered for permanent certification.

The blood disorders covered are haemophilia, thalassemia and sickle cell disorders. A benchmark disability of 40 per cent is prescribed for patients meeting the criteria for severe haemophilia, thalassemia major or intermedia, transfusion-dependent thalassemia intermedia, homozygous sickle cell disease and severe compound heterozygous sickle cell syndromes, including sickle-beta thalassemia and sickle-HbD.

For haemophilia, the criteria include factor VIII or IX levels -- clotting factors -- below five per cent, along with a history of two or more bleeds in major joints, one intracranial bleed or one muscle bleed.

For multiple disabilities, two or more specified conditions are assessed individually. Only disabilities of at least 25 per cent are included in the composite calculation.

The prescribed formula combines the higher and lower disability percentages. For instance, 40 per cent hearing disability and 30 per cent visual disability result in a composite disability of 58 per cent. The combined percentage cannot exceed 100.

Chronic neurological disorders, including Parkinson's disease and multiple sclerosis, are assessed across locomotor, visual, hearing, speech, cognitive and psychosocial impairments.

For epilepsy, the prescribed disability percentage is nil for a single convulsion (epileptic seizure episode), 25 per cent for one to five convulsions a month, 50 per cent for six to 10, and 75 per cent for more than 10 convulsions a month.

State governments and Union Territory administrations will designate persons with requisite qualifications and experience as certifying authorities for issuing disability certificates and Unique Disability Identity (UDID) cards.

The Director General of Health Services under the Health Ministry will decide cases involving doubts over interpretation of the definitions, classifications or evaluation procedures.

data.title: BSE Hospitals index soars 3%; Apollo, Max, Narayana Hrudayalaya surge 5%
data.description:
Hospital shares price movement

 
Shares of hospital companies extended their upward movement, with the BSE Hospitals index surging 3 per cent to 5,251.85 in Friday’s intraday deals on strong September quarter (Q2FY27) earnings and a healthy outlook.
 
In the past month, the BSE Hospitals index outperformed the market by soaring 20 per cent, against a 12.7 per cent rally in the BSE Sensex. The hospitals index quoted close to its record high of 5,498.15 touched on July 6, 2026. 
 
Apollo Hospital Enterprises, Max Healthcare Institute, Narayana Hrudayalaya and Rainbow Children's Medicare were up 5 per cent each on the BSE. Krishna Institute of Medical Sciences (KIMS), Jupiter Life Line Hospitals, Aster DM Quality Care, Fortis Healthcare and Global Health were up in the range of 2-3 per cent.
 
 
At 10:22 AM, the BSE Hospitals index was the top gainer among sectoral indices up 2.9 per cent at 5,229.86, compared to a 0.01 per cent decline in the BSE Sensex.
 

Why are hospital stocks outperforming the market?

 
Health Care Services reported a robust July to September quarter (Q2FY27), with India hospital sales growing 37 per cent year-on-year (YoY) and 19 per cent quarter-on-quarter (QoQ), led by strong patient volumes, steady average revenue per patient (ARPP) growth and merger & acquisition (M&A), Kotak Institutional Equities said in its result review.
 
Growth was broad-based, led by double-digit YoY volume growth across hospitals, with inorganic growth adding to Aster DM and Manipal. Cumulative India hospital earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortization (EBITDA) in the brokerage coverage grew 36 per cent YoY and 27 per cent QoQ, with EBITDA margin broadly stable YoY at 24.6 per cent and improving 140 bps QoQ, as new units ramped up, the brokerage firm said. It prefers Apollo Hospital, Narayana Hrudayalaya, Rainbow and Aster DM among hospitals.
 
Meanwhile, according to a CNBC report, global brokerage Macquarie upgraded Max Healthcare and Apollo Hospitals to 'Outperform' from 'Underperform', citing improving earnings prospects and more attractive valuations.
 
The brokerage believes consensus earnings estimate for the hospital sector have bottomed out, while valuations have moderated. It also believes the initial impact of profitability pressures from the ongoing bed expansion cycle is already reflected in stock prices, with newly added capacity ramping up at a healthy pace, the report said.
 

Why are Aster DM and Narayana Hrudayalaya in focus?

 
According to reports, Aster DM Quality Care is in discussions to purchase Northern India hospital assets from Narayana Hrudayalaya and the deal is expected to be valued at $150 million.
 
“This development is based on news sources speculation and for concrete decision making we would need confirmation from the respective companies,” ICICI Securities said in a note.
 
On the face of it, Aster DM has been looking to enter Northern India to increase its scale with a pan India presence. Its’ promoter Blackstone was among the front runners in acquiring a stake in Yatharth Hospitals; however the deal later fell apart. For Narayana, the Northern region contributes 13 per cent to the India business constituting 882 beds (15 per cent of the India business bed capacity) across Gurugram, New Delhi and Jaipur.
 
The brokerage firm believes that if Narayana decides to sell any of its’ North India assets, it could result in margin pressure on a consolidated levels due to nascent business integration with the recently acquired PPG Hospital in the UK. As this is an evolving situation with a few moving parts, the brokerage firm said it will keep a tab on how this deal pans out. Disclaimer: Views and outlook in this report belong to the brokerages and analysts cited. They do not reflect the views of Business Standard. Readers are advised to exercise discretion.
